questions.q: A 2×2 matrix $A = U\Sigma V^\top$ is applied to the unit circle. What are the lengths of the semi-axes of the resulting ellipse?
questions.explain: $V^\top$ only rotates/reflects the circle, $\Sigma$ stretches it to an axis-aligned ellipse with semi-axes $\sigma_1, \sigma_2$, and $U$ rotates it. Eigenvalues coincide in size only for symmetric matrices.

questions.q: For the shear $A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 1\\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$, how do singular values and eigenvalues compare?
questions.explain: The shear is triangular, so $\lambda = 1, 1$. But it is not symmetric: $\sigma_i^2$ are the eigenvalues of $A^\top A$, giving $\sigma \approx 1.618, 0.618$ (still $\sigma_1\sigma_2 = |\det A| = 1$).

questions.q: A 64×64 image has singular values $\sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2 \ge \dots$. By Eckart–Young, what is the Frobenius error of the best rank-$k$ approximation $A_k$?
questions.explain: Truncating the SVD drops the terms $\sigma_i u_i v_i^\top$ for $i>k$, and $\lVert A - A_k\rVert_F^2 = \sum_{i>k}\sigma_i^2$. The spectral-norm error is $\sigma_{k+1}$ — no rank-$k$ matrix does better.

questions.q: $A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 1\\ 1 & 1+\varepsilon\end{bmatrix}$ with tiny $\varepsilon$. Why is solving $Ax = b$ risky?
options: Because $\sigma_{\min}$ is tiny, so the condition number $\kappa = \sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}$ is huge and small errors in $b$ are amplified
It is not risky: $A$ is invertible for every $\varepsilon \neq 0$
questions.explain: Invertible is not the same as well-conditioned. With $\varepsilon = 10^{-6}$, $\kappa \approx 4\times10^6$: a nudge of 0.001 in $b$ moves $x$ by about 1000 in each component.
